first_boundary: An expired run is correctly rejected, but the submitted review was frozen with only the same failing retry. An absent-row lookup alone cannot safely release a delayed request.

browser_integration.expired_run_recovery: Real handler rejects the expired fixture run. Pointer and keyboard each cancel the exact request, obtain an unchecked new review, select a fresh fixture run, and accept exactly one new pairing. Retrying the cancelled request after its old fixture run becomes eligible still rejects.
browser_integration.storage_counts: Recovery leaves one encrypted cancellation record and one pairing; only that one pairing is accepted. Valid original-run cases retain one pairing and one issuance.
browser_integration.limits: Fixture browser identities, isolated pg-mem and fixture provider acceptance; not actual native human consent, real PostgreSQL concurrency, automatic host delivery or live gameplay.

preserved_invariants: The existing encrypted ledger owner/request unique slot arbitrates cancellation versus late issuance.
Cancellation records contain no destination, consent assertion, acceptance secret or authority.
An existing pairing is revoked through owner-authenticated CAS and durability checks, with original deadlines retained.
Lost cancellation replies keep the original request through reload; foreign owner and late owner/chat UI responses cannot affect another review.
Model-origin assertions do not authenticate the browser cancellation route.
No live approval, action lease, player assignment, source credential or run budget is created by cancellation.
